question: A 28-year-old man is brought unconscious after consuming an unknown substance. His GCS is 7, pupils are pinpoint, RR 8/min, BP 90/60 mmHg. Which is the MOST IMMEDIATE priority in his management?

answers.text: Administer activated charcoal to prevent further absorption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Activated charcoal is contraindicated in an unconscious patient with compromised airway — aspiration risk is severe.
Correct. GCS ≤8 with respiratory depression mandates airway protection first. Airway is always the first step in ABC stabilisation of the poisoned patient.

answers.text: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to identify cardiotoxic agents

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ECG is important but comes after securing airway and breathing — a dead airway cannot wait for an ECG.

answers.text: Send blood for toxicological screening before any intervention

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Investigations are important but resuscitation always precedes diagnosis in the ABC approach to poisoning.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the two simultaneous imperatives: resuscitation first, then identification. Airway is the first priority in the ABC approach.
Well done. In the poisoned patient, GCS ≤8 or any loss of protective airway reflexes demands immediate intubation before any other intervention.
